newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland back on Australian gold mining map.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland back on Australian gold mining map.

text.p: A number of new gold mines slated to come on stream later this year and in 1997 are securing Queensland's position as Australia's second largest gold-producing state, analysts and miners say.

"You just have to look at all the pegging that's taken place in the past two years to get an idea of the activity in Queensland," Harry Adams, the managing director of Devex Ltd, which is mining the Monkland deposit in Gympie.
Underground development and new mining technologies that enable old mines to be reworked are attracting more prospectors into the state, Morgan said.
Queensland produced 220,000 ounces of gold in the June quarter, second only to Western Australia with 1.76 million ounces, a tally by Bell Securities Ltd shows.
Western Australia still produces about 75 percent of Australia's gold , although rojects gearing should keep Queensland in the number two spot, analysts said.
"The growth in Queensland's profile is very strong," said Brett O'Donovan, analyst at Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones Ltd.
O'Donovan said some companies were finding it less competitive to obtain mining ground in Queensland.
"You haven't got the demand for ground as you do in Western Australia," O'Donovan said. "It's a lot easier for companies to peg ground here."
As more gold is prosppected in Queensland, O'Donovan expects the number of local publicly-trade mining conmpanies to rise.
"It definetly will change, we just need some exciting deposits," O'Donovan said.
Currently, stock exchange gold explorers listings are dominated by Western Australia companies.

New mines helping raise Queensland's profile include the high-grade Vera Nancy project, 50-50 owned by Battle Mountain Gold Co and Normandy Mining Ltd, which expects to be producing at an annual rate of between 90,000 to 100,000 ounces a year by August 1997.
Battle Mountain has proposed a US$40 million capital development programme for Vera Nancy, which includes upgrading of a processing plant and site infrastructure work.
MIM Holdings Ltd Sarsfield project in central Queensland will commence production in December 1997 at an annual rate of 150,000 ounces a year.
MIM's Ernest Henry mine north east of Cloncurry also is gearing up to start production next year at an annual rate of 120,000 ounces.
Mining companies with bigger names in Western Australia are starting to show more interest in Queensland as well.
Acacia Resources Ltd, Sons of Gwalia Ltd, Great Central Mines Ltd and Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd all have exposure in the state.

Meanwhile, a feasibility study is due in the current quarter on development of the Mount Rawdon deposit 75 km southwest of Bundaberg, 85 percent owned by Placer Pacific Ltd, with the remaining stake held by Resolute Samantha Ltd.
Increases in production also are expected from several smaller mining companies, including Devex.
In August, Devex announced a five-fold increase in gold ore reserves and the discovery of a highly mineralised deposit at its underground mining operations at Gympie in South East.
Devex's Morgan said Gympie produced about 100 tonnes of gold between 1867 and 1927 and has the potential to regain a high profile in the mining industry.
Gold production in the Northern Territory totalled 157,000 ounces in the June quarter, followed by 85,000 ounces in New South Wales, according to Bell Securities.
